steps.body: Solids **move** differently! Round parts **roll**. Flat parts **stack** and **slide**. A ball rolls. A cube stacks.
Some solids roll. Some stack. Some do both.

widget.prompt: Tap every solid that can ROLL.

hotspots.label: box
hotspots.feedback: A box has flat faces all the way round, so it slides — it cannot roll.

widget.missFeedback: A solid rolls if it has a round, curved part to roll on.
widget.successFeedback: The ball, the can and the cone all have a curved side to roll on. The box has only flat faces, so it slides instead.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents roll stack slide.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for roll stack slide must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines roll stack slide.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

steps.body: A cylinder does **both**: on its side it rolls; on its flat end it stacks, like cans at the store.

explanationVariants: Cubes have flat sides everywhere, so they stack into towers and never roll.
Flat all around means stack, not roll.

widget.prompt: Which solid stacks into a tower but cannot roll? Tap it.

hotspots.label: sphere
hotspots.feedback: A sphere ONLY rolls — no flat side to stack on. The stacker is the cube.

hotspots.label: cylinder
hotspots.feedback: A cylinder stacks AND rolls on its side — the one that never rolls is the cube.

hotspots.label: cone
hotspots.feedback: A cone rolls in circles on its side — the never-roller is the cube.

widget.missFeedback: Think about which sides are flat and which are round, then tap the solid.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — flat sides stack; no round part to roll.

widget.prompt: Sort each solid: can it roll?

items.label: ball (sphere)
items.feedback: Round all over — it rolls every way.

items.label: dice (cube)
items.feedback: Flat sides all around — it tips but never rolls.

items.label: can (cylinder)
items.feedback: On its side, a can rolls in a line.

items.label: block (cube)
items.feedback: All flat — blocks stack, never roll.

widget.missFeedback: Think: does it have a ROUND part? Round parts roll.
widget.successFeedback: Sorted — round parts roll, flat parts stay!

explanationVariants: A cylinder's flat circle ends sit on each other, so cans stack in towers.

widget.prompt: Cans stack at the store. Which part makes stacking work?

options.label: The flat circle ends
options.feedback: Yes — flat ends sit steady on each other.

options.label: The round side
options.feedback: The round side ROLLS — the flat ENDS do the stacking.

options.label: The label
options.feedback: Paper does not hold a tower up — the flat ends do.

options.label: Cans cannot stack
options.feedback: They can! Their flat ends stack tall towers.

explanationVariants: A cone rolls on its side — but in a circle around its point.
Pointy end anchors it: a cone rolls in circles.

widget.prompt: Which solid rolls in a CIRCLE around its own point? Tap it.

hotspots.label: cube
hotspots.feedback: A cube cannot roll at all — the circler is the cone.

hotspots.label: sphere
hotspots.feedback: A sphere rolls straight any way — the circler is the cone.

hotspots.label: cylinder
hotspots.feedback: A cylinder rolls in a straight line — the circler is the cone.

widget.missFeedback: Think about which sides are flat and which are round, then tap the solid.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — the point stays put while the wide end circles around.

explanationVariants: Spheres have no flat side — the tower tumbles. Cubes stack best.
Flat-sided cubes stack; round spheres roll away.

widget.prompt: You want the TALLEST tower. Tap the blocks you should pick.

hotspots.label: spheres
hotspots.feedback: Balls roll right off each other — pick flat-sided cubes.

hotspots.label: cones
hotspots.feedback: Points cannot hold the next block — cubes stack best.

widget.missFeedback: Cubes stack wonderfully — flat on flat!
widget.successFeedback: Yes — flat sides stack steady and tall.

hints: Stacking needs flat tops and bottoms.
Which solid is flat on EVERY side?
Cubes — flat everywhere, perfect for towers.

steps.body: Round parts roll. Flat parts stack and slide.
takeaways: Spheres roll every way; cubes never roll.
Cylinders roll on their side AND stack on their ends.
Cones roll in circles around their point.

concept.body: Round parts roll. Flat parts stack. A ball rolls; a cube stacks; a can does both.

explanationVariants: A ball is round all over, so it rolls.

widget.prompt: Which solid rolls every way you push it?

options.label: Sphere
options.feedback: Yes — round all over rolls all ways.

options.label: Cube
options.feedback: Flat sides stop it — the all-way roller is the sphere.

options.label: Cone
options.feedback: A cone circles its point — the all-way roller is the sphere.

options.label: Cylinder
options.feedback: A cylinder rolls one way only — the all-way roller is the sphere.
